sentences.text: The crime was registered on the allegation that accused Nos. 1 and 2 made it appear that M/s. Krishna Finance & Associates, an institution registered under the MSMED Act, 2006 in the name of the 2 nd accused, is the sister concern of Aikya Mahila Co-operative Society, Ulloor, of which the petitioner is the president.

It is alleged that by creating such an impression, the 1 st accused collected Rs.20 lakhs from CW1 to CW6 by offering them permanent employment in the establishment and thereafter failed to provide the promised job or to CRL.MC NO. 7682 OF 2025 2025:KER:73988 return the money.
According to the prosecution, the illegal acts were committed in connivance with the petitioner.
2. Learned Counsel for the petitioner contends that, even if the prosecution allegations are accepted in their face value, the ingredients of cheating are not made out against the petitioner.

It is the contention of the learned Counsel that the Secretary of the Mahila Society is the custodian of all records and use of the Society's stationery by the other accused cannot result in the petitioner's implication by reason of her being the president of the Society.
3. Learned Public Prosecutor submitted that the contentions now urged cannot be considered in a proceeding under Section 528 of BNSS.

sentences.text: In spite of the strenuous efforts of the learned Counsel for the petitioner, I am not inclined to CRL.MC NO. 7682 OF 2025 2025:KER:73988 invoke the inherent power under Section 528 of BNSS, since consideration of the contentions urged calls for appreciation of evidence.
It is the settled law that, for the purpose of invoking the inherent power, the High Court should not conduct a mini trial or microscopic scrutiny of documents.
Moreover, the petitioner has an effective remedy of moving the trial court for discharge.
5. The Crl.M.C is hence closed, reserving the petitioner's right to move the trial court for discharge and directing the court below to pass a reasoned order on the discharge petition, if filed.
6. Learned Counsel then submitted that the petitioner may be permitted to move the discharge application in absentia.
In support of the said prayer, reference is made to Annexure A-6 treatment records.
Having gone through the treatment records, I find the request to be well founded.
Hence, the court CRL.MC NO. 7682 OF 2025 2025:KER:73988 below is directed to consider the petition for discharge without insisting on the petitioner's presence.

Sd/-
